title: GTIN — Global Trade Item Number
objectives: Understand GTIN via a real-life analogy

sections.markdown:
**Think of a GTIN as the passport number for a product.**

Every unique product SKU sold in the world of retail carries a Global Trade Item Number — a number that identifies the *product itself*, not the physical box. Two identical 500 g packs of Amul butter share the same GTIN. A 1 kg pack of Amul butter has a **different** GTIN. A carton of 12 × 500 g packs (a case) has yet another GTIN (a GTIN-14 with an *indicator digit* saying 'this is a case').

- **GTIN is a NUMBER, not a barcode.** The barcode is one way to carry the number; you could also print it in ink, embed it in a URL, or NFC it.
- **Globally unique** — GS1 gives your company a **GCP** (Global Company Prefix); you assign the remaining digits to your products. No collisions worldwide.
- **Four lengths** — 8, 12, 13, 14 digits. All are stored/exchanged padded to 14 digits with leading zeros.
- **Check digit** — the last digit is a mod-10 checksum that catches most scanning errors.
- **Not a serial number.** A GTIN tells you *WHAT the item is* (Amul butter 500g). A serial number tells you *WHICH INDIVIDUAL BOX*. Serialization requires SGTIN — GTIN + serial via AI (21).

**Why every retail Flutter app must speak GTIN fluently:** scan barcode → parse GTIN → look up product in your catalog. Get the check-digit validation wrong and every wrong number crashes the flow. Get the length normalization wrong and cross-catalog joins fail silently.

**GTIN (Global Trade Item Number)** is a GS1-assigned numeric identifier for a trade item — a product intended to be priced, ordered, or invoiced at any point in the supply chain. Four forms: **GTIN-8** (small items, GS1 country-assigned), **GTIN-12** (UPC-A, primarily North America), **GTIN-13** (EAN-13, primarily Europe + rest of world), **GTIN-14** (cases / cartons, uses an indicator digit). All GTINs are equivalent when padded to 14 digits. Last digit = mod-10 check digit.
## GTIN variants at a glance

## GTIN-14 anatomy

```
1  8901234  567895  2
│  │        │       └── check digit
│  │        └────────── item reference (assigned by brand owner)
│  └─────────────────── GCP (Global Company Prefix from GS1)
└────────────────────── indicator digit (0 = consumer unit, 1-8 = packaging level, 9 = variable measure)
```

**Indicator digit** — allows a brand owner to create a hierarchy: `0` for the individual can, `1` for the 6-pack, `2` for the case, `3` for the pallet, all sharing the same GCP + item reference.

## India-specific notes

- Indian GCPs typically start with **890** (assigned by GS1 India). A GTIN starting `890` = manufactured/registered in India.
- FSSAI + BIS regulations increasingly require GS1-registered GTINs on packaged food + medical devices.
- Pharmaceutical DPDPA + drug traceability rules use GS1 DataMatrix (GTIN + batch + expiry + serial).
- **Never assume country from GCP alone** — the GTIN tells you WHERE it was registered, not WHERE it was made or sold.
## Common mistakes
**Mistake 1: Storing without padding.** DB has `8901234567895` (13 digits); the sync partner sends `08901234567895` (14 digits) — cross-catalog joins silently miss. Normalize on ingest.
**Mistake 2: Skipping check-digit validation.** A user typo in a manual-entry field passes through; the scan flow works but the catalog lookup fails. Validate at boundaries.
**Mistake 3: Truncating leading zeros.** Excel opens the CSV, drops the leading zero, product data corrupted. Always TEXT-typed GTIN columns; never numeric.
**Mistake 4: Confusing GTIN with SKU.** SKU is internal — 'SKU-123'. GTIN is external + globally unique. Both fields on the product row.
**Mistake 5: Using GTIN as a serial number.** GTIN identifies the product TYPE. To identify an individual physical box, use **SGTIN** (GTIN + AI 21 serial).
**Mistake 6: Restricted-Circulation Numbers (2xx / 04-09) treated as global.** GTINs starting with 2 (in-store) or 04-05 are internal-only + reused across chains. Filter or flag.
**Mistake 7: Ignoring indicator digit on GTIN-14.** Case GTIN and consumer GTIN look similar but are different products; the indicator makes the difference.
**Mistake 8: Assuming barcode format = GTIN length.** DataMatrix can carry a GTIN-14; EAN-13 carries a GTIN-13. Barcode ≠ number.
## Best practices
**1. GTIN-14 canonical form** in your DB.
**2. Validate check digit at every entry point** — scan, import, manual entry.
**3. TEXT column** — never numeric; never Excel-imported without quoting.
**4. Index the GTIN column** for fast catalog lookup.
**5. Store BOTH SKU (internal) + GTIN (external)** on the product.
**6. Flag restricted / in-store GTINs** — don't sync to external partners.
**7. Track hierarchy** — consumer unit + case + pallet all as separate rows with links.
**8. Log invalid-GTIN scan attempts** — catalog gaps + scanner-hardware issues.

## Interview Q&A

**Q1: What exactly does a GTIN identify + how is that different from a serial number?**

**A:** A GTIN identifies a **product type** (a stock-keeping unit): 'Amul butter 500g salted.' Every physical unit of that SKU has the same GTIN. A **serial number** identifies a *specific physical unit*: 'this exact box, made on 2026-06-30, batch B7'. In GS1, serial numbers are combined with a GTIN via **AI (21)** to form an **SGTIN** — `Serialized GTIN`. Pharmacies + medical devices + high-value electronics use SGTIN because they must track each unit through the supply chain. Grocery + FMCG use plain GTIN because tracking each individual can is overkill. **Interview red flag:** confusing GTIN with SKU or with serial. **Signal of depth:** knowing that GS1's AI (01) is GTIN + AI (21) is serial + AI (10) is batch/lot + AI (17) is expiry.

**Q2: How does the mod-10 check digit work + why bother?**

**A:** Algorithm: reading the number RIGHT-TO-LEFT (ignoring the check digit), alternately multiply each digit by 3 and 1, sum, mod 10, subtract from 10, mod 10 → check digit. Catches ~90% of single-digit errors and adjacent-digit transpositions (`53` typed as `35`). **Why bother:** scanners misread; users typo. A single-digit corruption without a check digit silently maps to a DIFFERENT valid product; with the check digit, ~90 % of corruptions are caught. In retail, a wrong scan = wrong price / wrong inventory decrement = money loss + audit nightmare. **Also required by GS1 standards** — any GTIN without a valid check digit is *not* a GTIN. Validate at every boundary.

**Q3: Why store as GTIN-14 canonical form?**

**A:** GS1 documentation calls out GTIN-14 as the **exchange format** for supply-chain messages. If your DB stores GTIN-13 for local products but a supplier sends GTIN-14 (with leading `0` for consumer units, `1-9` for cases), your join silently fails to match. **Rule:** normalize all inputs to GTIN-14 on ingest (pad left with 0). This: (1) simplifies joins with external systems; (2) allows hierarchical products (consumer unit + case + pallet) to be stored the same way; (3) makes indexing predictable. **Cost:** minor — 14-char strings are cheap. **Alternative:** store 8/12/13/14 as-is + normalize on every query — brittle + performance hit. Interviewers score highly on this specific answer.

**Q4: What is a restricted-circulation number + why does it matter for imports?**

**A:** GTIN prefixes **2** (used for in-store products — weighed items, private-label SKUs) and **04-09** (varies by GS1 country policy) are **not globally unique** — they're allocated for in-store or internal use and can be reused by different retailers. **Implication:** if you ingest a `2xxxxxxxx` GTIN from your retail POS + try to look it up in a global catalog (Amazon, GS1 Registry), it will collide with another retailer's assignment. **Handle:** flag the GTIN as `restrictedCirculation: true` at ingest; do NOT sync to external partners; do NOT trust as a global identifier. Retailers use these for in-store weighed items (a `20xxxxxxxx` on a cheese label encodes price/weight, not identity). Not knowing this leads to catalog data pollution + wrong-partner integrations. Interviewer bonus signal.

**Q5: How would you handle GTIN hierarchies (consumer + case + pallet) in a data model?**

**A:** Three linked rows: (1) consumer unit GTIN-14 (indicator=0, e.g., 500 g pack); (2) case GTIN-14 (indicator=2, e.g., 12-pack); (3) pallet GTIN-14 (indicator=3, e.g., 40 cases). Each is a separate row in `products`; a `packaging_hierarchy` table links parent GTIN → child GTIN with a `pack_quantity` column (12, 40). **Query patterns:** scan a case GTIN → look up children → decrement inventory; scan a consumer unit → look up parent → identify case identity. **Serial flow:** SGTINs are attached to consumer units; the case's serial (**SSCC**) contains references to the SGTINs it holds — this is the digital-twin backbone for pharma track-and-trace. Interviewers respect this end-to-end grasp.

**Q6: What are common Indian regulatory + retail considerations for GTINs?**

**A:** **(1) GS1 India assigns GCPs starting with 890.** Companies register + pay annual fees. **(2) FSSAI** (Food Safety) increasingly encourages GS1 codes on packaged food for traceability. **(3) BIS / drug regulations** — Ministry of Health mandates GS1 DataMatrix on Schedule H1 drugs + medical devices (with GTIN + batch + expiry + serial). **(4) Export rules** — some countries reject imports without GS1-registered GTINs; India-made goods for export must ensure GCP is legitimate. **(5) Duplicates / counterfeits** — anti-counterfeit initiatives use GS1 Digital Link (product-authentication URL). **(6) Restricted-circulation** — private-label products use 890 GCPs from GS1 India (not `2` prefix which is in-store). **Practical impact for apps** — Indian retail + pharma + food supply chain apps depend on correct GTIN handling; wrong data = compliance + audit problems.

## Real-world usage

- **Retail POS** — scan → GTIN lookup → price + inventory.
- **E-commerce** — GTIN in product listing schema.org markup (Google demands it).
- **Pharma** — GTIN + batch + expiry in DataMatrix; regulatory traceability.
- **Supply chain** — case/pallet GTIN-14 in shipping documents.
- **India export** — GS1 India-issued GCPs mandatory for many export markets.
- **NOT for** — internal SKUs / stock codes (use a separate SKU field).

## Advanced notes

- **AI (01)** = GTIN in a GS1 element string.
- **`ai:'01'`** in GS1 Digital Link URLs.
- **Variable-measure GTIN** — indicator digit `9` marks weight/price-embedded codes.
- **GTIN restrictions** — 240-259 range (GTIN-12/13 prefixes) is reserved.
- **GS1 Registry** — global catalog of GTIN → brand-owner + product name.
- **VerifiedByGS1** — brand owners verify their own GTINs; consumer apps can query.
- **GLN vs GTIN** — GLN identifies parties + locations; GTIN identifies products.
- **Historic UPC-E** — 6-digit compressed UPC-A; expand to UPC-A on ingest.
- **Reused GTINs** — GS1 discourages but allows after 48 months of no supply-chain activity.
- **Data quality** — verify GTIN existence via GS1 Verified or the brand owner's authoritative service before trusting.
- **Migration** — apps built pre-2005 sometimes stored EAN-13 as 13-char TEXT; upgrade to GTIN-14 padded during a schema migration.
- **Barcode symbology encoding** — UPC-A encodes GTIN-12; EAN-13 encodes GTIN-13; ITF-14 encodes GTIN-14; DataMatrix + QR encode any via AI (01).
